app.js:10 Total is summed from unrounded float prices while each line shows a price rounded to 2 places, so the displayed lines do not add up to the displayed total. Price is stored as typed (app.js:18, :20) and only rounded when displayed (app.js:8). The money rule lives in render, in floating point, with no rounding to cents. Driven: lines 1 x 5.00 and 3 x 1.00 (price 1.005) display a total of 8.02 where the lines show 8.00. The unrounded 1.005 is what is posted to the server. Add a line with price 1.005 and quantity 3: the row reads '3 x 1.00' but the total contributes 3.02. The invoice total contradicts its own lines, and the server receives sub-cent prices.

app.js:26 JSON body is sent without a Content-Type header, so it goes as text/plain. fetch with a string body defaults to Content-Type: text/plain;charset=UTF-8. No headers option on app.js:26. The server is not in the payload, so the parsing side is inferred. A server that parses JSON by content type (for example express.json()) ignores the body: req.body is empty, so the invoice is created empty or rejected with 400 even though the lines were valid.

app.js:8 render builds HTML by string interpolation, and escapeHtml does not escape double quotes. l.client is inserted into the title="..." attribute. A client name like x" onmouseover="alert(1) is not escaped, because escapeHtml handles only & < >, so it breaks out of the attribute and injects an event handler (XSS). The fix is to also escape " and ', or to use textContent/setAttribute.

guards.js:21 Double-send guard is a 1-second timer, not an in-flight guard; a slow request can be sent twice. guards.js:21-26 only compares Date.now() to the previous click. app.js:25-26 has no in-flight flag, no disabled button, no idempotency key. The lines array is not cleared after a successful send (app.js:28), so a second POST carries the same content. On a 3 s response, the user clicks Send at t=0, sees nothing happen (no feedback, see the other finding), and clicks again at t=1.5 s. tooSoon() returns false, a second POST /api/invoices is issued with the same lines. The client is invoiced twice. Even after success, clicking again after 1 s resends the same invoice.

app.js:19 Validation accepts any positive price, including Infinity and values with extra decimals, and does not bound qty. Number('1e999') is Infinity, which passes price > 0. The total then becomes 'Infinity'. A huge qty such as 99999999999999999999 is accepted, so the total loses precision. Float arithmetic on money (qty * price summed) gives rounding errors, for example 0.1*3.
